source.title: On the Over-Memorization During Natural, Robust and Catastrophic Overfitting
source.authors: Runqi Lin; Chao-Jian Yu; Bo Han; Tong-Liang Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study intervenes on high-confidence training patterns and measures changes in natural-training generalization gaps, using a different method from the claim versions. It does not test their specific settings or mechanisms.
record.gate_note: Natural-training results on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN, Tiny-ImageNet, and CIFAR-10 ViT bear on the generalization-gap claim. Adversarial robustness results are outside the claim's natural-label scope. No version's specific claim is directly tested.
record.test_reason: The study tests its own account of over-memorization and DOM interventions, but none of V1–V8. High confidence and persistent low loss are not random-label memorization (V1) or inclusion-based label memorization (V8). No experiment varies width, convolutional versus fully connected architecture, optimizer, batch size, dropout, or magnitude-aware sharpness as the versions require.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' main conclusion: sudden high-confidence predictions and persistent memory constitute a shared over-memorization behavior across natural, robust, and catastrophic overfitting, motivating DOM removal or augmentation. Their conclusion also includes corresponding natural/adversarial confidence and acknowledges dependence on augmentation quality. The empirical improvements are not universal: DOMDA with AUGMIX fails to prevent catastrophic overfitting on CIFAR-100, and some appendix results improve final error while increasing best-to-final deterioration.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses its own DOM removal and iterative augmentation interventions, rather than the original methods specified in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The generalization-gap changes vary with pattern group, augmentation, dataset, architecture, and checkpoint. The paper reports that removal of original high-confidence patterns worsens the gap, while removal of transformed high-confidence patterns improves it.

fits_no_version.finding: On naturally trained CIFAR-10 PreactResNet-18, removing all high-confidence patterns reduces the reported training–test gap from 4.84% to 4.63%; removing originally high-confidence patterns increases it to 5.57%, while removing newly high-confidence patterns reduces it to 4.42%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization effect of removing high-confidence patterns depends on when they became high-confidence.

fits_no_version.finding: Transformed high-confidence patterns show only an approximately 0.01 training-loss increase after their removal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Patterns that become high-confidence around natural overfitting can retain persistent low loss after exclusion from training.

fits_no_version.finding: In Table 2, DOM filtering and augmentation lower mean final test error and reduce best-to-final deterioration relative to their paired baselines; best-checkpoint error does not improve in every comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Confidence-based filtering or iterative augmentation can improve final test performance and reduce late-training deterioration in image classifiers.

record.problems: The paper reports the random-seed standard deviations for tabulated results, but Section 3.1's pattern-removal results are text and figure descriptions without stated uncertainty. It does not test random-label memorization or the specific architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, width, sharpness, or example-influence claims in the versions.
record.rows_left_out: Adversarial-training and robustness outcomes are not cataloged because the claim excludes out-of-distribution and adversarial robustness results. Figure-only detailed curves and hyperparameter ablations are also omitted because they do not supply recoverable numeric values in the text.

untested.parts: Paired random-label and natural-label training, near-perfect random-label fitting, and chance held-out performance on random labels.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD-based optimizers under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations, their association with training–test gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Selection by inclusion-based label memorization, retraining after removal, and comparison with equally sized random removals. Confidence-based filtering does not supply these tests.

record.verdict_notes: No listed version receives a verdict. Table 2's Diff is Best minus Last test error, despite the paper calling it a generalization gap; it differs from Section 3.1's training–test gap. Reported uncertainties are standard deviations over three seeds, not significance tests. Omitted appendix DOM results do not bear on V1–V8, so they require no missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting, chance test accuracy on random labels, and the stated architectures and recipes.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error as a function of width.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer comparisons and tuning conditions.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons to norm- or margin-based measures.
The study removes high-confidence patterns, not examples selected by their measured contribution to correct prediction; it does not compare removal with random-example removal.

rows.subject: PreactResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Removed all high-confidence training patterns after the first learning-rate decay (All-HC).
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The text describes a noticeable improvement of 4% and a gap reduction from 4.84% to 4.63%.
rows.check: The 4.84% to 4.63% gap reduction is correctly reported but tests no listed version; partial is therefore inapplicable.

rows.subject: PreactResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Removed original high-confidence patterns (Ori-HC).
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The text says this removal negatively affects generalization; the baseline gap is stated elsewhere as 4.84%.
rows.check: Baseline should be 4.84%. Removing originally high-confidence patterns raises the reported gap to 5.57%, but this is not removal selected by inclusion-based memorization with retraining and a random-removal control (V8).

rows.subject: PreactResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Removed transformed high-confidence patterns (Trans-HC).
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The text says this removal effectively alleviates natural overfitting.
rows.check: Baseline should be 4.84%. The reduction to 4.42% concerns transformed high-confidence patterns, not V8's memorization-selected examples.

rows.subject: PreactResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Removed all high-confidence patterns; measured the training-loss change for removed transformed high-confidence patterns.
rows.measure: Increase in training loss after removal
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The authors use the barely increased loss as evidence of persistent memory.
rows.check: The approximately 0.01 loss increase measures persistent memory after removal. It measures neither random-label fitting nor inclusion-based memorization and test-accuracy loss.

rows.subject: PreactResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Natural training baseline, no DOM intervention.
rows.uncertainty: ± values reported for Best and Last
rows.note: The table reports Best and Last test error and their Diff; it does not define the sign convention for Diff in the supplied text.
rows.check: Contextual baseline only. Augmentation is standard random cropping and horizontal flipping, not none. Diff is Best minus Last test error, not the training–test gap; its sign is recoverable from the numbers.

rows.subject: PreactResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: DOMRE training on a strict subset of natural patterns.
rows.uncertainty: ± values reported for Best and Last
rows.note: Authors state DOMRE consistently outperforms baselines at the final checkpoint and reduces the generalization gap.
rows.check: Own-method performance comparison, not a test of a listed version. DOMRE dynamically excludes low-loss patterns after warm-up and permits relearning when loss rises; it is not permanent example removal followed by retraining.
